name: The Inverse Hook
description: Start by showing what everyone does wrong. The viewer watches because they want to know if they're the problem.
structure:
SHOT 1: Show the wrong thing being done
SHOT 2: Hard cut — 'That's why your planning application failed'
SHOT 3–N: The correct approach, step by step
SHOT FINAL: CTA
example_hook: This is the one drawing that kills most planning applications before they're even read.

name: The Costly Mistake Inverse
description: Open on a finished renovation that looks right — then reveal the expensive mistake hidden in it.
structure:
SHOT 1: Finished, polished result
SHOT 2: 'This extension cost £40k more than it needed to'
SHOT 3–N: Where the money went — and what they should have done
SHOT FINAL: CTA
example_hook: This kitchen extension looks perfect. It cost £18,000 more than it should have.

name: Myth Bust
description: State the wrong belief as if it's fact, then dismantle it with evidence. Works because the viewer holds the belief.
structure:
SHOT 1: 'Everyone thinks you need planning permission for this'
SHOT 2: The data or rule that breaks the myth
SHOT 3–N: What you actually need — and what that means for them
SHOT FINAL: CTA
example_hook: Everyone thinks a loft conversion always needs planning permission. Most don't.

name: Stat Drop
description: Open cold with a number that stops the scroll. No context — just the stat. Then explain why it matters.
structure:
SHOT 1: The stat, no explanation
SHOT 2: Why this number matters to THIS viewer
SHOT 3–N: What to do with it
SHOT FINAL: CTA
example_hook: 67% of UK home extensions run over budget. Same reason every time.

name: Step Reveal
description: Give the viewer a framework they can act on today. One step per shot. Ends with the full picture.
structure:
SHOT 1: 'Three things architects check before drawing anything'
SHOT 2–4: One clear step each
SHOT 5: Combine — 'Now you have a brief'
SHOT FINAL: CTA
example_hook: Three things your architect checks before drawing a single line.

name: Before / After
description: Lead with the transformation. Show the result first, then walk back to the start.
structure:
SHOT 1: The stunning after
SHOT 2: 'Here's what it looked like before'
SHOT 3–N: The journey — constraints, decisions, pivots
SHOT FINAL: CTA
example_hook: This became a 4-bed family home. It started as a £200k terraced with a dead-end layout.

name: Client Journey
description: Follow a real client decision from confusion to clarity. The viewer sees themselves in it.
structure:
SHOT 1: 'My client was about to make a £30k mistake'
SHOT 2: The brief they came in with
SHOT 3–N: What changed and why
SHOT FINAL: CTA
example_hook: My client came to me with full planning approval. I told them to pause.

name: Personal Story
description: First person. Specific moment. The lesson lands harder when it's personal.
structure:
SHOT 1: The specific moment — 'I walked into a site last week'
SHOT 2–N: What happened and what it revealed
SHOT FINAL: CTA
example_hook: I walked into a client's house last week and immediately knew the extension quote was wrong.

name: The Three-Way Challenge
description: Give three people the same problem. The reveal drives comments about who the viewer agrees with.
structure:
SHOT 1: 'I gave three homeowners the same £80k budget'
SHOT 2–4: What each one did
SHOT 5: The outcome — who came out ahead
SHOT FINAL: CTA
example_hook: Same house. Same £80k. Three totally different decisions.

name: Can You Spot It?
description: Show something on screen and ask the viewer to find the problem before you reveal it. Comment bait.
structure:
SHOT 1: 'What's wrong with this floor plan? Comment before I tell you.'
SHOT 2: Hold on the image
SHOT 3: The reveal
SHOT FINAL: CTA
example_hook: What's wrong with this floor plan? Most architects miss it first time.

name: Build the Tension
description: Create a slow reveal. Each shot adds a layer. The payoff lands harder because of the wait.
structure:
SHOT 1: 'I need to show you something'
SHOT 2–N: Progressive build — 'And here's why that matters...'
SHOT FINAL: The reveal + CTA
example_hook: This planning decision changed everything. I need to show you why.

name: The Slow Cost Reveal
description: Show a renovation line item by line item. Viewer stays for the total.
structure:
SHOT 1: 'Here's what a two-storey extension actually costs — broken down'
SHOT 2–N: Each cost line, building up
SHOT FINAL: The total + CTA
example_hook: Let's break down exactly what a two-storey extension costs. Stay till the end.

name: Bad Advice vs Good Advice
description: Play two voices — the bad advice the internet gives and the professional reality. Comedic contrast.
structure:
SHOT 1: 'What Google says about loft conversions'
SHOT 2: 'What actually happens'
SHOT 3: 'What Google says...'
SHOT 4: 'What actually happens'
SHOT FINAL: CTA
example_hook: What Google says about planning permission vs what actually happens.

name: The Contractor Script
description: Voiceover plays a dodgy contractor. You respond as the architect. The contrast is the joke.
structure:
SHOT 1: Contractor voice: 'You don't need an architect for that'
SHOT 2: Adam: 'Here's what that costs you'
SHOT 3–N: Evidence
SHOT FINAL: CTA
example_hook: "You don't need an architect for that." That phrase costs homeowners £15k on average.

name: The Diagnostic Question
description: Open with a question that makes the viewer diagnose their own situation. Personalisation drives saves.
structure:
SHOT 1: 'Are you planning a loft conversion? Ask yourself this first'
SHOT 2–N: The diagnostic framework
SHOT FINAL: CTA
example_hook: Planning a loft conversion? Three questions that will save you from a costly mistake.

name: The Contrarian Take
description: State something that contradicts what your audience has been told. The disruption creates curiosity.
structure:
SHOT 1: 'Stop trying to add value to your home'
SHOT 2: 'Here's what you should actually be doing'
SHOT 3–N: The reframe
SHOT FINAL: CTA
example_hook: Stop trying to add value to your house. It's the wrong goal.

name: The Unpopular Opinion
description: Lead with a position most people disagree with. The controversy drives comments.
structure:
SHOT 1: 'Unpopular opinion: most planning applications are written to fail'
SHOT 2: The argument
SHOT 3–N: The evidence
SHOT FINAL: CTA
example_hook: Unpopular opinion: most homeowners should rent while they renovate.

name: The Countdown
description: Promise a number of things at the start. The viewer stays to collect them all.
structure:
SHOT 1: '5 things your contractor will never tell you'
SHOT 2–6: One per shot
SHOT FINAL: CTA
example_hook: 5 things your contractor won't tell you before the quote.

name: The Cost Comparison
description: Compare two approaches side by side. Budget, timeline, outcome. The viewer picks a side.
structure:
SHOT 1: 'Extend vs move — I ran the numbers for a 3-bed in Birmingham'
SHOT 2: Option A costs
SHOT 3: Option B costs
SHOT 4: The verdict
SHOT FINAL: CTA
example_hook: Extend vs move. I ran the real numbers for a 3-bed in Birmingham.

name: Rules Breakdown
description: Take a dense rule (planning, building regs, etc.) and make it actionable in under a minute.
structure:
SHOT 1: The rule most people get wrong
SHOT 2: What the rule actually says
SHOT 3: What it means for you specifically
SHOT FINAL: CTA
example_hook: Permitted development rights — what they actually cover and what they don't.
